//: How an environment tells the agent what it has.
The image cannot know that THIS seat has a vector store, a credential CLI or a browser grid.
So the environment declares them here and the boot discovers them at start - then PROBES each
one before letting the agent believe it. A tool that fails its probe is dropped from the reflex
table rather than left as a lure toward something that is gone.
The field that matters is `when`. A registry keyed by tool name answers 'what do I have'; a
registry keyed by SITUATION answers 'what do I do now', which is the only question an agent
actually asks. An entry without a `when` is rejected at load.
`trap` is the tempting wrong move the tool replaces. Naming it is what stops the agent doing
This file is an EXAMPLE. Replace the entries with your own; nothing here is required.

tools.name: ripgrep
tools.when: searching many files for a string
tools.trap: recursive grep over a whole tree, or reading files one at a time to look for it

tools.name: jq
tools.when: reading one field out of a JSON response
tools.trap: dumping the whole object and reading past the rest - which is how a neighbouring secret leaks

tools.name: git
tools.when: asking what actually changed, or whether you have been here before
tools.trap: assuming the current state is the intended state
